JUDGMENT
The Petitioners have filed these two petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a road accident dated 15.07.2020.
Both the petitions have arisen out of a common accident.
Therefore, both the petitions have been clubbed SCCH-25 together as per order dated 16.11.2021 for common trial and common judgment is passed.

2. The case of the Petitioners in brief is as follows: That on 15.07.2020 at about 10.30 am after finishing the work at Tiptur and in order to return, the petitioners were proceeding in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA44M1621, which was driven by Kruthik S Gowda on the extreme left side of the Road via Nonavinakere.

While so proceeding they reached near Alburu Pond Turning, Alburu,
Nonavinakere Hobli, Tumakuru, suddenly the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01C3105 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life, without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and came to his extreme right i.e., wrong side and dashed against the petitioners' Indica Car.
Consequent to the terrific impact, both sustained grievous injuries.
SCCH-25 3
. It is the further case of the Petitioner Mr.Subramanya T.J. (in MVC No.4364/2020) that immediately after the accident he was shifted to Turuvekere Govt. Hospital.

After first aid treatment, due to severe injuries sustained by him for further treatment he was referred to Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Research Center, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, wherein the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient, underwent wound debridement and skin graft and after necessary treatment he was discharged with an advise for follow up treatment.

sentences.text: So far he has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/ towards medicine, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental expenses etc.,
Prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as a Software Engineer at IBM Net Connect, Bangalore, earning a sum of Rs.40,000/ per month.

Due to the aforesaid accidental injuries, he cannot see objects properly and sight is blur, getting head ache and giddiness, cannot walk long distance, cannot SCCH-25 stand long time, cannot lift or carry weight from the ground, cannot ride vehicle and he has undergone deep mental shock, pain and sufferings,
since the injuries caused to him are permanent in nature.

Therefore, the Respondents being the RC owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
5. In response to notices issued by this tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels.
But the respondent No.2 alone filed written statement.

6. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
The Respondent No.2 in the written statement has stated that the petition is not maintainable either on law or on facts.
It has denied the issuance of policy in respect of SCCH-25 the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01C3105 in the alleged accident.
It is submitted that the drivers of both Lorry and Car did not have valid DL.
The owner of the Lorry has willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not have valid and effective DL.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary party.
There is non compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The Respondent insurer has further denied the age, occupation, income and other details of the Petitioners and has sought for dismissal of the petitions.

7. 2.

sentences.text: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA01C3105, the petitioners have SCCH-25 examined themselves as PWs.1 & 2 and got marked 5 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.4 & P.6.
They have reiterated the contents of the petition in their affidavits filed in lieu of chief examination.
The Respondent No.2 insurer has denied the issuance of policy in respect of the Lorry bearing No.KA01C3105 and contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary party.
In the cross examination of Pws.1 & 2, nothing worthwhile showing the absence of negligence on the part of the offending vehicle driver is elicited.

12. The nature of damages to the vehicle as per Ex.P.4 MVA report shows that the vehicle bearing No.KA44 M1621: (1) MV front right side mirror, bonnet, bumper, body wind shield glass and frame, right side window (Driver), shock absorber, right side wheel, wheel guard, right side chassis damaged.

(2) MV right side front and left side rear left side body scratched and dented and the following damages were found at the time of investigation of the SCCH-25 vehicle bearing No.KA 01C3105: (1) MV front right side corner scratched to the mirror of the body.
This shows that the right front portion of the Car is entirely damaged, where the Lorry has suffered only a scratch.
During the chief examination of Pws.1 & 2, they have stated that the Lorry hit their Car due to which the vehicle was damaged.
This shows that the Car was hit by the Lorry and also supports the case of the petitioners.
The other documents at Exs.P.1 to 4 and P.6 i.e., FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, MVA report and charge sheet are in accordance with the statements given by the petitioners.

As such,
there are no reasons to discard or disbelieve the version of the Petitioners/Pws.1 & 2.

This shows that on account of the accident the Petitioners have sustained grievous and simple injuries respectively.
As per Ex.P.4, the accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the motor vehicles.

Therefore, on SCCH-25 overall perusal of Exs.P.1 to 4 & P.6 it is clear that the accident occurred on 15.07.2020 and the petitioners sustained injuries as mentioned in Exs.P.5 & 12 and the sole reason for the occurrence of the accident was rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing No.KA 01C3105.
Accordingly, issue No.1 in both the cases are held in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2 In MVC 4364/2020

: The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accidental injury, he suffered Traumatic injury to right periorbital region with tissue loss over upper eyelid, full thickness skin loss of 80% upper lid, abrasion over forehead and right perioribital region,
sever injuries to hand and leg which are grievous in nature.
He is suffering from pain and agony and also suffered financial loss, since the injuries have caused permanent disability.
The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the SCCH-25 accidental injuries and that he is suffering from permanent disability

has examined Mr. Govindaraju J - Medical Record Officer at Adichunchanagiri Hospital as PW.3 and produced 4 documents as per Exs.P.24 to 27 authorization letter, copy of accident register extract, copy of police intimation and inpatient case sheet.
During the cross of PW.3 nothing worthwhile is elicited.
But the petitioner has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note SCCH-25 that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.5 discloses that, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/ under the head of Pain and Suffering.
The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,
In this regard he has produced 43 medical bills for a sum of Rs.74,726/.
There is no contrary evidence to these medical bills from the respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Turuvekere Govt. Hospital and thereafter at Aadichunchanagiri Hospital and Research centre, B.G.Nagara as an inpatient from 16.07.2020 to 01.08.2020.

LIABILITY:
The respondent No.2 examined Sri.Prashanth as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.4, Authorization letter, cancelled Cheque, Bank endorsement and letter sent to the owner of the vehicle.
The contention of the respondent No.2 SCCH-25 is that even though the insurance was issued to the offending Lorry, the Cheque given by the owner/Respondent No.1 was dishonored for insufficient funds.
During the cross examination of RW.1, nothing has been elicited by the counsel for petitioner to show that the policy was in existence.
17. A policy of insurance is a contract between the insurance company and the insured.
A valid contract requires passing of proper consideration.
However, in this case, the Cheque given has been returned for funds insufficient as per Bank Endorsement dated 04.04.2020 at Ex.R.3.
In addition the insurance company has given a notice dated 22.04.2020 seeking for remitting the premium and informing about nonrealization of the Cheque.
But as per records the Respondent No.1 has neither replied to Ex.R.5 nor paid the premium.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident there was no valid contract between the insured and the insurer.
In the case on hand Respondent SCCH-25 No.1 was represented by a counsel but except filing Vakalath, he has neither filed written statement nor led any evidence.
This shows utter negligence on the part of the respondent No.1.
However, the respondent No.2 has proved that it has taken all steps for revival of the policy.
It has also proved that it is not under any liability to the petitioners due to the absence of a valid contract.

Therefore,
the respondent No.1 is solely responsible to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 in both the cases are held in the affirmative.

SCCH-25 18. Issue No.3 in both the cases:
In view of above answers to the above issues, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petitions in MVC No.4364/2020 and MVC No.4365/2020 are hereby allowed with cost.
The petitions are dismissed as against the Respondent No.2.
The Respondent No.1 being the RC owner is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount to the Petitioners within 60 days from today.

The Petitioner in MVC. No.4364/2020 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,35,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Five Thousand) along with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.
SCCH-25

The Petitioner in MVC. No.4365/2020 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.30,000/ (Rupees Thirty Thousand) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.

On deposit of compensation and interest in both the cases, entire amount shall be released to the petitioners in both the cases in their respective names by way of e payment with due acknowledgment and proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/ in each case.

The original copy of this judgment is ordered to be kept in MVC.4364/2020 and the copy of it be kept in MVC.4365/2020.
Office to draw separate awards accordingly.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
